_comment: Real, public X accounts that post XRP/FXRP calls. `scripts/ingest-x.ts` reads this list.
⚠️ These are real people, so three rules apply that do not apply to seeded data:
1. Only their own posts count. Retweets and replies are dropped by the ingester —
amplifying someone else's call is not making one, and scoring it against them
would be a fabricated attribution.
2. No wallet goes in without a self-disclosure URL (HANDOFF.md §2.2). None of these
have one here, so `wallet` stays null and said-vs-did correctly reports
'no wallet disclosed' rather than inferring anything.
3. Every stored post keeps its real platform id and URL, and `synthetic = 0`, so the
UI links to the actual post and a reader can check the extraction against it.
To add someone: append a handle. To remove them from the demo, delete the entry and
re-run the ingester with --reset.
⚠️ Two cohorts here, and the difference is the whole point.
The first 19 were chosen by hand as well-known XRP commentators. Measured: 55 of their
posts classified produced ZERO scored calls — they post news, sentiment and promos, and
the nine that came closest sat at 0.80 against the 0.85 bar. Those nine were a greeting
("GM XRP MILLIONAIRES"), a Starbucks platitude, and third-party news. The bar was NOT
lowered to convert them; that would have put invented P&L on real named people.
The rest came from `npm run find-callers`, which searches for the SHAPE of a call and
keeps only authors whose priceable asset is the SUBJECT of the post.
⚠️ Rejected from that sweep, and why it matters: @SchmidtTi0, @Leoncrypto_1,
@Globalfcap, @Bruno_negrao and @Cryptobeall___ all rank highly on hit count, but they
post calls on unpriceable alts ($INX, $HOT, $VELVET, $ARPA, $SAPIEN) while spamming
"$BTC $ETH $XRP $SOL" as hashtag decoration. The cashtag is not the subject, so scoring
them would attribute an $INX trade to BTC — a fabricated call, which is exactly what this
list exists to prevent. Also rejected: "$X Target price for Tomorrow👀 <link>" accounts,
which state no target anywhere in the text.
